fields.rationale: States cluster primarily around how they define the practice experience threshold (years vs. hours), whether they emphasize exam passage as a central hurdle, or whether they rely mainly on a broad equivalency/good-standing standard with few additional conditions.

assignments.raw_value: Applicant must hold current, valid, unrevoked license in state with equivalent standards; be engaged in active practice for 5 years or 5,000 hours; pass jurisprudence exam; have no pending disciplinary action; submit affidavits from two licensed dentists; provide official transcript; meet other criteria as required by board rule.
Five years of continuous practice in another state, territory, District of Columbia, or Canada with equivalent proficiency standards

Applicant must have passed clinical examination of another state or testing agency more than five years prior, maintain substantially equivalent licensure standards, meet minimum active practice hours, and complete continuing education requirements of jurisdiction where licensed

Applicant must hold an active and unrestricted license from another U.S. state/territory, have at least five years of active clinical practice or equivalent, no disciplinary history, no recent exam failures, 50 units of CE within two years, and meet other documentation requirements.

Current valid license in good professional standing from another state or territory with commensurate standards; continuous work as licensed dentist in academic or clinical setting for at least one year immediately preceding application

Must have current licensure in good standing in another state, District of Columbia, or U.S. territory; for dentists, must have 3 years of active dental practice in another jurisdiction; for dental hygienists, must have practiced minimum 3 of last 5 years; must pass Delaware jurisprudence and National Board exams; must meet all requirements of § 1122(c)(2) through (c)(7)

Applicants for provisional license by credentials must have been in full-time clinical practice or full-time faculty for five years immediately preceding the application and must hold an active dental license in good standing from another state. Must pass clinical examination given by state or regional testing agency and jurisprudence examination.

Applicant must hold a license from a similar dental board of another state with equivalent requirements, have passed a regional or national examination approved by the dental board or have been in legal practice for three consecutive years immediately prior to filing the application, and furnish other evidence of qualifications as required by the board.

Five years of clinical practice with minimum 3,500 hours, graduation from ADA-accredited dental school, successful completion of national board dental examinations, and successful completion of board-approved clinical examination

Applicant must have been lawfully licensed in another state/territory with equivalent standards, engaged in practice for at least 2 years, and provide certificate of good moral character from licensing board

Licensed in another state with substantially equal requirements; practiced dentistry for at least 2 of the 3 years preceding application; passes law examination; completed required continuing education hours in previous 2 years
Applicant must have held a license in another state for five years immediately preceding application and engaged in active practice of dentistry for at least five years prior to application

Applicant must have been lawfully in practice for at least five years in another state, present a certificate of registration and duration of practice from that state's board of dental examiners or equivalent, and the other state must require a degree of competency equal to that required in Massachusetts.
Must pass ADLEX and Maryland Dental Jurisprudence Examination, or have 5 years active practice with clinical exam and comprehensive written exam

Applicant must hold a valid, substantially equivalent license in good standing for at least 3 consecutive years immediately preceding the application, or demonstrate substantially similar qualifications. Board may also issue a temporary license for 6 months upon showing a valid out-of-state license.
Applicant must substantially meet Michigan requirements, be licensed in a state/province with substantially equivalent standards, and may be required to appear personally for an interview.

Must have passed all components of National Board Dental Examinations; been in active practice at least 2,000 hours within 36 months; currently licensed in another state or Canadian province without pending/final disciplinary action; good moral character; pass English proficiency test at board discretion; meet other credentialing requirements.

Licensed in another state for at least five consecutive years; qualifications at least equivalent to Missouri requirements; at least 21 years of age; good moral character and reputation. Board may require examination on Missouri laws and practical examination if licensure was denied, revoked, or suspended for incompetency.

Currently hold a valid, unrestricted and unexpired license in a state whose standards for licensure are determined by the board as equivalent to Mississippi's standards, and which state grants reciprocity or licensure by credentials to licensees of the State of Mississippi; active practice for past five years; no pending disciplinary action; passed state or regional clinical licensure examination within past five years
Applicant must be licensed in good standing in another state, have required education and training, pass satisfactory examinations, and meet other Board requirements

Five years of active practice in good standing in another jurisdiction with substantially equivalent requirements; grounds for denial do not exist; payment of board-determined fee; certificate from every jurisdiction where licensed; passage of written examination on North Dakota laws and rules; and any other requirements established by board rule

Must meet board standards under section 38-126 and have been actively engaged in the practice of dentistry for at least one year under a license in another state, territory, or the District of Columbia. Practice in an accredited school or college of dentistry for completing a postgraduate or residency program also counts.
Requirements or standards for certification or licensure in another state must be equivalent to or greater than New Hampshire requirements

Applicant must have been licensed and practiced dentistry for at least five years immediately preceding the application; must present proof by affidavit; must present a certificate from the board of dental examiners of the prior state certifying competency and good moral character; certificate must be presented not more than six months after its date of issue; and the issuing state must recognize certificates from NJ in like manner.

Applicant must hold active license in another state, have been in practice for at least 5 years, not have had license suspended or revoked, not have been refused a license, not be involved in pending disciplinary action, pay applicable fees, and submit statement regarding child support compliance

Applicant must file an application, meet educational requirements, have satisfactory experience, pass an examination, be at least 21, be a US citizen or lawful permanent resident, and be of good moral character as determined by the department.

Applicant must hold a license in another state or have satisfactory work experience, government certification, or private certification in a state that does not issue a license, as described in Chapter 4796

A dentist holding a general dentist license in good standing and having practiced for at least five hundred (500) hours within the previous five (5) years immediately prior to application and having passed a regional examination substantially equivalent to the requirements for this state may apply for licensure by credentials

Applicants with active practice in other states for at least 3,500 hours in the five years preceding application may satisfy examination requirements through regional and national testing agencies or clinical board examinations administered by other states

Applicants licensed in other states may obtain licensure by credentials if they have actively practiced for 5 years, passed a state or regional clinical board examination and jurisprudence exam, completed 70 hours of continuing education over 5 years, and have no disciplinary history

Applicant must have graduated from an ADA-accredited dental school, completed minimum 3,000 clinical hours within 5 years, passed national comprehensive and clinical exams, hold valid license in another state, have no disciplinary proceedings, meet equivalent or higher licensure requirements, provide good moral character references, and pass state laws examination

Applicant must hold valid license in another state, have no pending disciplinary charges, have not failed Tennessee exam previously, be ADA-accredited graduate, demonstrate intent to practice in Tennessee, and meet experience requirements (5 years practice/teaching or 2 years practice plus equivalent exam)

Applicant must be licensed in good standing in another state with substantially equivalent requirements, have no pending disciplinary actions, have graduated from a CODA-accredited school, passed a recognized national examination, passed the board's jurisprudence examination, submitted CPR certification, practiced for at least 3 years, and been endorsed by the board of dentistry in the jurisdiction where the applicant practices.

Applicant must be currently licensed in good standing with an unrestricted license in another jurisdiction, document having met all requirements for licensure except the degree requirement, and document having been successfully engaged in clinical practice as a dentist for not less than 6,000 hours in the five years immediately preceding the date of application for licensure.

Must hold current unrestricted license in another U.S. jurisdiction, be in good standing, have not committed acts constituting grounds for denial, and have been in continuous clinical practice for five of the six years immediately preceding application

Applicant must be licensed in good standing in another U.S. or Canadian jurisdiction with substantially equivalent requirements, complete an approved emergency office procedures course, pass the dentist jurisprudence examination, and meet active practice requirements. For jurisdictions with non-equivalent requirements, applicant must have at least 5 years of full-time licensed practice at 1,200+ hours per year.

Applicant must hold a valid license and be currently engaged in practice in another state, and either (a) be a graduate of a dental college approved by the commission, or (b) have practiced in another state for at least four years and completed a one-year postdoctoral residency approved by the commission.
Must meet requirements for licensure established by the examining board by rule, submit evidence of current CPR/AED proficiency, and present the license and pay the applicable fee.
